Holistically-Nested Edge Detection, retrained in TensorFlow

This notebook retrains HED (Xie & Tu, ICCV 2015) in TensorFlow/Keras, following the authors' original Caffe recipe, and exports weights that load directly into my hed-tensor library. It downloads its own data and runs end to end on Kaggle.

Result: ODS F-score 0.782 on BSD500 · Trained on 2× Tesla T4

PyPI: hed-tensor

HED on Kaggle: train on T4 + export for hed-tensor¶

TensorFlow/Keras re-training of Holistically-Nested Edge Detection (Xie & Tu, ICCV 2015) following the authors' Caffe recipe (s9xie/hed). Exports weights that drop straight into the hed-tensor library. One notebook: it downloads its own data.

Runs on Kaggle with GPU T4 x2 and internet on. SMOKE_TEST = True does a quick end-to-end check before the full run.

Same as the Caffe recipe (solver.prototxt, train_val.prototxt): labels = round(gt/255) (only edges most annotators agree on) · class-balanced sigmoid cross-entropy summed over pixels for the 5 side outputs + fuse · SGD momentum 0.9, weight decay 2e-4 on weights only · per-layer learning rates (conv1-4 ×1, conv5 ×100, side outputs ×0.01, fuse ×0.001, biases ×2) · base lr 1e-6, ÷10 every 10k updates · 10 images per update · side outputs start at 0, fuse at 0.2.

Different: 'same' padding + bilinear resize instead of Caffe's pad=35 + deconvolution + crop (the layer layout of hed-tensor, so the weights stay compatible). The 10 images of an update are same-size images split over the GPUs instead of 10 accumulated single images: identical gradient, VGG has no batch norm.

Outputs (/kaggle/working): export/ (weights for the library), checkpoints/, logs/, figures/, predictions/*.zip.

Settings¶

import os
from pathlib import Path

SMOKE_TEST = False  # True: tiny end-to-end run (a few minutes) to check everything before the real run
SMOKE_TEST = SMOKE_TEST or os.environ.get('HED_SMOKE_TEST') == '1'  # (used for local testing)

# Training recipe
EPOCHS = 10                # 10 x 28,800 images ≈ the paper's 30k updates x 10 images
BATCH_SIZE = 10            # images per update (Caffe iter_size=10)
BASE_LR = 1e-6
LR_STEP_UPDATES = 10_000   # Caffe lr_policy "step": lr x LR_GAMMA every 10k updates
LR_GAMMA = 0.1
MOMENTUM = 0.9
WEIGHT_DECAY = 2e-4
LABEL_THRESHOLD = 128      # gt >= 128 is an edge, same as Caffe's round(gt/255)
SEED = 7

LOG_EVERY_UPDATES = 100
MAX_TRAIN_HOURS = 10.5     # checkpoint and move on to export before Kaggle's 12 h limit

if SMOKE_TEST:
    EPOCHS, LOG_EVERY_UPDATES = 1, 2
    SMOKE_TRAIN_IMAGES, SMOKE_TEST_IMAGES = 100, 6

DOWNLOADS = {  # file name: (url, exact size in bytes)
    'HED-BSDS.tar': ('https://vcl.ucsd.edu/hed/HED-BSDS.tar', 1_303_992_320),
    'vgg16_weights_tf_dim_ordering_tf_kernels_notop.h5': (
        'https://storage.googleapis.com/tensorflow/keras-applications/vgg16/vgg16_weights_tf_dim_ordering_tf_kernels_notop.h5', 58_889_256),
}

1. GPUs¶

Each update's 10 images are split in halves: on T4 x2 one half per GPU in parallel, on a single GPU the two halves run one after the other (keeps memory well inside 16 GB).

In [2]:
os.environ.setdefault('TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL', '1')

import time

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras

build = tf.sysconfig.get_build_info()

      f'| built for {build.get("cuda_compute_capabilities")}')

2. Data, VGG16 weights, hed-tensor¶

Downloads the HED-BSDS training set (1.3 GB, UCSD) and the ImageNet VGG16 weights, resumable with retries and checked against their exact size. If the files are in an attached input (for example the old dependency-pack notebook), those are used instead. hed-tensor (your library) is installed to check the exported weights.

In [3]:
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request


def find_input(name):
    hits = sorted(INPUT.rglob(name)) if INPUT.exists() else []
    return hits[0] if hits else None


def _fetch(url, part):
    """Download url into part, resuming from what is already there."""
    have = part.stat().st_size if part.exists() else 0
    headers = {'Range': f'bytes={have}-'} if have else {}
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers), timeout=60) as r:
        if have and r.status != 206:  # server ignored the range request: start over
            have = 0
        total = have + int(r.headers.get('Content-Length') or 0)
        done, next_report = have, have
        with open(part, 'ab' if have else 'wb') as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 20):
                f.write(chunk)
                done += len(chunk)
                if total > 50e6 and done >= next_report:
                    print(f'    {part.name[:-5]}: {done / 1e6:,.0f} / {total / 1e6:,.0f} MB')
                    next_report = done + total // 10


def download(url, dest, size, tries=5):
    if dest.exists() and dest.stat().st_size == size:
        return dest
    part = dest.with_name(dest.name + '.part')
    for attempt in range(1, tries + 1):
        try:
            _fetch(url, part)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'    attempt {attempt}/{tries} failed: {e!r}')
        got = part.stat().st_size if part.exists() else 0
        if got == size:
            break
        if got > size:  # corrupt partial file
            part.unlink()
        time.sleep(5 * attempt)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f'could not download {url}')
    part.rename(dest)
    return dest


def get_file(name):
    url, size = DOWNLOADS[name]
    found = find_input(name)
    if found is not None and found.stat().st_size == size:
        print(f'{name}: using attached input {found}')
        return found
    t0 = time.time()
    path = download(url, DATA / name, size)
    print(f'{name}: downloaded ({size / 1e6:,.0f} MB, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)')
    return path


if not list(DATA.rglob('train_pair.lst')):
    tar = get_file('HED-BSDS.tar')
    t0 = time.time()
    subprocess.run(['tar', '-xf', str(tar), '-C', str(DATA)], check=True)
    print(f'unpacked HED-BSDS.tar in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s')
HED_ROOT = next(DATA.rglob('train_pair.lst')).parent
VGG_WEIGHTS = get_file('vgg16_weights_tf_dim_ordering_tf_kernels_notop.h5')
print('data:', HED_ROOT)

try:

except ImportError:
    cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '-q', '--no-deps']
    r = subprocess.run(cmd + [HED_TENSOR], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode and find_input('hed_tensor-1.0.1-py3-none-any.whl'):  # no internet: wheel from an attached input
        r = subprocess.run(cmd + [str(find_input('hed_tensor-1.0.1-py3-none-any.whl'))], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(r.stderr)
    import hed_tensor
print('hed_tensor', hed_tensor.__version__)

3. Data pipeline¶

The 28,800 augmented training pairs come in only 27 image sizes, so each batch is filled with images of one size: no padding or resizing. Batches are reshuffled every epoch. The 200 BSDS500 test images (test/ in HED-BSDS) are used for progress figures and predictions.

In [4]:
import random
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

MEAN_BGR = np.array([104.00699, 116.66877, 122.67892], np.float32)  # Caffe HED / VGG mean, BGR order

pairs = [l.split() for l in (HED_ROOT / 'train_pair.lst').read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
if SMOKE_TEST:
    pairs = pairs[:SMOKE_TRAIN_IMAGES]  # few image sizes, so full batches of BATCH_SIZE
IMG_PATHS = np.array([str(HED_ROOT / img) for img, _ in pairs])
LBL_PATHS = np.array([str(HED_ROOT / lbl) for _, lbl in pairs])

t0 = time.time()
by_size = defaultdict(list)
for i, path in enumerate(IMG_PATHS):
    by_size[Image.open(path).size].append(i)  # reads the header only
print(f'{len(pairs):,} training pairs in {len(by_size)} image sizes ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)')


def epoch_order(epoch):
    """Image indices for one epoch; every run of BATCH_SIZE consecutive indices has one image size."""
    rng = random.Random(SEED * 1000 + epoch)
    batches = []
    for idx in by_size.values():
        idx = idx[:]
        rng.shuffle(idx)
        batches += [idx[i:i + BATCH_SIZE] for i in range(0, len(idx) - BATCH_SIZE + 1, BATCH_SIZE)]
    rng.shuffle(batches)
    return [i for b in batches for i in b]


UPDATES_PER_EPOCH = len(epoch_order(0)) // BATCH_SIZE
TOTAL_UPDATES = EPOCHS * UPDATES_PER_EPOCH


def load_pair(img_path, lbl_path):
    img = tf.io.decode_image(tf.io.read_file(img_path), channels=3, expand_animations=False)
    img = tf.cast(img[..., ::-1], tf.float32) - MEAN_BGR          # RGB → BGR, minus mean
    gt = tf.io.decode_image(tf.io.read_file(lbl_path), channels=1, expand_animations=False)
    return img, tf.cast(gt >= LABEL_THRESHOLD, tf.float32)


def make_dataset(epoch):
    order = epoch_order(epoch)
    ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((IMG_PATHS[order], LBL_PATHS[order]))
    ds = ds.map(load_pair, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE, deterministic=True)
    return ds.batch(BATCH_SIZE).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)


TEST_PATHS = [HED_ROOT / l.split()[0] for l in (HED_ROOT / 'test.lst').read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
if SMOKE_TEST:
    TEST_PATHS = TEST_PATHS[:SMOKE_TEST_IMAGES]


def load_test(path):
    """RGB uint8 image and the model input (1, H, W, 3)."""
    rgb = np.array(Image.open(path).convert('RGB'))
    return rgb, (rgb[..., ::-1].astype(np.float32) - MEAN_BGR)[None]


images, labels = next(iter(make_dataset(0)))
print(f'{UPDATES_PER_EPOCH:,} updates per epoch, {TOTAL_UPDATES:,} total | first batch {images.shape}, '
      f'edge pixels {float(tf.reduce_mean(labels)):.1%} | {len(TEST_PATHS)} test images')

4. Model¶

Same attribute names and layer order as hed_tensor.HED (block1..5, dsn1..5, fuse), so model.save_weights() gives a file the library loads unchanged. Only the starting values follow Caffe.

In [5]:
from tensorflow.keras import layers


class HED(keras.Model):
    def __init__(self, vgg_weights=None):
        super().__init__()
        vgg = keras.applications.VGG16(weights=vgg_weights, include_top=False)
        get = vgg.get_layer

        def pool():
            return layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2, 2), strides=(2, 2), padding='same')

        self.block1 = keras.Sequential([get('block1_conv1'), get('block1_conv2')])
        self.block2 = keras.Sequential([pool(), get('block2_conv1'), get('block2_conv2')])
        self.block3 = keras.Sequential([pool(), get('block3_conv1'), get('block3_conv2'), get('block3_conv3')])
        self.block4 = keras.Sequential([pool(), get('block4_conv1'), get('block4_conv2'), get('block4_conv3')])
        self.block5 = keras.Sequential([pool(), get('block5_conv1'), get('block5_conv2'), get('block5_conv3')])
        # Caffe: side outputs have no filler (start at 0), the fuse layer starts at 0.2
        self.dsn1, self.dsn2, self.dsn3, self.dsn4, self.dsn5 = (
            layers.Conv2D(1, 1, padding='same', kernel_initializer='zeros') for _ in range(5))
        self.fuse = layers.Conv2D(1, 1, padding='same', kernel_initializer=keras.initializers.Constant(0.2))

    def call(self, x, training=False):
        """training=True: logits of the 5 side outputs + fuse. training=False: sigmoid(fuse)."""
        h, w = tf.shape(x)[1], tf.shape(x)[2]
        c1 = self.block1(x)
        c2 = self.block2(c1)
        c3 = self.block3(c2)
        c4 = self.block4(c3)
        c5 = self.block5(c4)
        sides = [self.dsn1(c1)] + [tf.image.resize(dsn(c), [h, w], method='bilinear')
                                   for dsn, c in ((self.dsn2, c2), (self.dsn3, c3), (self.dsn4, c4), (self.dsn5, c5))]
        fused = self.fuse(tf.concat(sides, axis=-1))
        return (*sides, fused) if training else tf.nn.sigmoid(fused)

    def blocks(self):
        return [self.block1, self.block2, self.block3, self.block4, self.block5]

    def dsns(self):
        return [self.dsn1, self.dsn2, self.dsn3, self.dsn4, self.dsn5]


model = HED(vgg_weights=str(VGG_WEIGHTS))
model(tf.zeros([1, 64, 64, 3]))
print(f'{sum(int(np.prod(v.shape)) for v in model.trainable_variables) / 1e6:.2f}M parameters')

14.72M parameters

5. Loss and Caffe-style SGD¶

Loss per output = Caffe's HED SigmoidCrossEntropyLoss: edge pixels weighted by the fraction of non-edge pixels and vice versa, summed over the image, averaged over the images in the update. Total = 5 side outputs + fuse.

Update (Caffe SGD, per parameter): v = momentum·v + lr·lr_mult·(grad + weight_decay·decay_mult·w), w -= v.

The training log also shows each loss relative to chance (an output that always says 0.5): 1.0 = guessing, lower is better. Raw summed losses jump around with the number of edge pixels per batch; the ratio doesn't. Expect a short spike above 1 in the first updates (momentum + conv5's 100x learning rate), as in Caffe.

In [6]:
import math


def balanced_bce(labels, logits):
    """Per-image Caffe HED loss, shape (batch,)."""
    bce = tf.nn.sigmoid_cross_entropy_with_logits(labels=labels, logits=logits)
    n_all = tf.cast(tf.reduce_prod(tf.shape(labels)[1:]), tf.float32)
    n_pos = tf.reduce_sum(labels, axis=[1, 2, 3])
    loss_pos = tf.reduce_sum(labels * bce, axis=[1, 2, 3])
    loss_neg = tf.reduce_sum((1.0 - labels) * bce, axis=[1, 2, 3])
    return loss_pos * (n_all - n_pos) / n_all + loss_neg * n_pos / n_all


def chance_loss(labels):
    """Per-image balanced_bce of an output that always says 0.5."""
    n_all = tf.cast(tf.reduce_prod(tf.shape(labels)[1:]), tf.float32)
    n_pos = tf.reduce_sum(labels, axis=[1, 2, 3])
    return 2.0 * math.log(2.0) * n_pos * (n_all - n_pos) / n_all


def caffe_param_groups(model):
    """(variable, lr_mult, decay_mult) as in s9xie/hed train_val.prototxt."""
    convs = [(l, 100.0 if blk is model.block5 else 1.0)
             for blk in model.blocks() for l in blk.layers if isinstance(l, layers.Conv2D)]
    convs += [(dsn, 0.01) for dsn in model.dsns()] + [(model.fuse, 0.001)]
    groups = [g for layer, m in convs for g in ((layer.kernel, m, 1.0), (layer.bias, 2 * m, 0.0))]
    assert len(groups) == len(model.trainable_variables)
    return groups


VARS, LR_MULTS, DECAY_MULTS = zip(*caffe_param_groups(model))
MOMENTA = [tf.Variable(tf.zeros_like(v), trainable=False) for v in VARS]
UPDATE = tf.Variable(0, dtype=tf.int64, trainable=False)  # updates done (saved in checkpoints)
EPOCH = tf.Variable(0, dtype=tf.int64, trainable=False)   # epochs done


@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None, None, None, 3], tf.float32),
                              tf.TensorSpec([None, None, None, 1], tf.float32),
                              tf.TensorSpec([], tf.float32)])
def train_step(images, labels, lr):
    """One Caffe SGD update on the whole batch, computed in len(DEVICES) parts."""
    n = tf.cast(tf.shape(images)[0], tf.float32)
    losses, chance, grads, prev = 0.0, 0.0, None, None
    for k, (dev, x, y) in enumerate(zip(DEVICES, tf.split(images, len(DEVICES)), tf.split(labels, len(DEVICES)))):
        # parts on the same GPU run one after the other, so only one part's activations are in memory
        with tf.device(dev), tf.control_dependencies(grads if k and dev == prev else []):
            with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
                part = tf.stack([tf.reduce_sum(balanced_bce(y, out)) for out in model(x, training=True)]) / n
                total = tf.reduce_sum(part)
            part_grads = tape.gradient(total, VARS)
        grads = part_grads if grads is None else [a + b for a, b in zip(grads, part_grads)]
        losses += part
        chance += tf.reduce_sum(chance_loss(y)) / n
        prev = dev
    for v, g, m, lr_mult, decay_mult in zip(VARS, grads, MOMENTA, LR_MULTS, DECAY_MULTS):
        if decay_mult:
            g = g + WEIGHT_DECAY * decay_mult * v
        m.assign(MOMENTUM * m + lr * lr_mult * g)
        v.assign_sub(m)
    return losses, chance


@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([1, None, None, 3], tf.float32)])
def predict_all(x):
    """Sigmoid maps of the 5 side outputs + fuse for one image."""
    return [tf.nn.sigmoid(o) for o in model(x, training=True)]


print(f'lr multipliers: {sorted(set(LR_MULTS))}')

lr multipliers: [0.001, 0.002, 0.01, 0.02, 1.0, 2.0, 100.0, 200.0]

6. Train¶

Checkpoint (weights + momentum + counters) after every epoch, kept in checkpoints/. A progress figure on 3 test images is saved per epoch.

In [7]:
import csv
import shutil

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

if not (CKPT_DIR / 'checkpoint').exists() and find_input('checkpoint') is not None:
    prev_run = find_input('checkpoint').parent.parent  # .../checkpoints/checkpoint of an attached earlier version
    shutil.copytree(prev_run / 'checkpoints', CKPT_DIR, dirs_exist_ok=True)
    if (prev_run / 'logs/train_log.csv').exists():
        shutil.copy(prev_run / 'logs/train_log.csv', LOG_DIR)
    print('copied checkpoint from attached input', prev_run)

ckpt = tf.train.Checkpoint(model=model, momenta=MOMENTA, update=UPDATE, epoch=EPOCH)
manager = tf.train.CheckpointManager(ckpt, CKPT_DIR, max_to_keep=2)
if manager.latest_checkpoint:
    ckpt.restore(manager.latest_checkpoint).assert_existing_objects_matched()
    print(f'resumed {manager.latest_checkpoint}: {int(EPOCH.numpy())} epochs, {int(UPDATE.numpy()):,} updates done')
else:
    print('starting from ImageNet VGG16')

PREVIEW = TEST_PATHS[:3]


def save_progress_figure(epoch):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, len(PREVIEW), figsize=(4 * len(PREVIEW), 6))
    for col, path in enumerate(PREVIEW):
        rgb, x = load_test(path)
        axes[0, col].imshow(rgb)
        axes[1, col].imshow(1 - predict_all(x)[-1].numpy()[0, ..., 0], cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=1)
    for ax in axes.flat:
        ax.axis('off')
    fig.suptitle(f'fused output after epoch {epoch}')
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / f'progress_epoch_{epoch:02d}.png', dpi=80)
    plt.close(fig)


LOG_PATH = LOG_DIR / 'train_log.csv'
if not LOG_PATH.exists():
    LOG_PATH.write_text('update,epoch,lr,loss,dsn1,dsn2,dsn3,dsn4,dsn5,fuse,chance,img_per_s\n')

update, start_epoch = int(UPDATE.numpy()), int(EPOCH.numpy())
session_start, stopped_early = time.time(), False
print(f'training epochs {start_epoch + 1}..{EPOCHS}, {TOTAL_UPDATES - update:,} updates to go')
with open(LOG_PATH, 'a', newline='') as log_file:
    log = csv.writer(log_file)
    for epoch in range(start_epoch, EPOCHS):
        window, n_images, t_window = [], 0, time.time()
        for b, (images, labels) in enumerate(make_dataset(epoch)):
            lr = BASE_LR * LR_GAMMA ** (update // LR_STEP_UPDATES)
            window.append(train_step(images, labels, tf.constant(lr, tf.float32)))
            update += 1
            n_images += int(images.shape[0])
            if update % LOG_EVERY_UPDATES:
                continue
            losses = tf.reduce_mean(tf.stack([l for l, _ in window]), axis=0).numpy()
            chance = float(tf.reduce_mean(tf.stack([c for _, c in window])))
            if not np.isfinite(losses).all():
                raise FloatingPointError(f'loss became {losses} at update {update}')
            speed = n_images / (time.time() - t_window)
            eta_min = (TOTAL_UPDATES - update) * BATCH_SIZE / speed / 60
            log.writerow([update, round(epoch + (b + 1) / UPDATES_PER_EPOCH, 4), lr, losses.sum(), *losses, chance,
                          round(speed, 1)])
            log_file.flush()
            print(f'epoch {epoch + 1}/{EPOCHS}  update {update:,}/{TOTAL_UPDATES:,}  loss {losses.sum():,.0f}  '
                  f'vs chance: fuse {losses[-1] / chance:.2f}x, sides {losses[:5].mean() / chance:.2f}x  '
                  f'lr {lr:.0e}  {speed:.0f} img/s  ETA {eta_min:.0f} min')
            window, n_images, t_window = [], 0, time.time()
            if time.time() - session_start > MAX_TRAIN_HOURS * 3600:
                stopped_early = True
                break
        UPDATE.assign(update)
        if stopped_early:
            manager.save()
            print(f'Stopped after {MAX_TRAIN_HOURS} h, checkpoint saved. Attach this version as input and run again to finish '
                  f'(the unfinished epoch restarts). Continuing with export of the current weights.')
            break
        EPOCH.assign(epoch + 1)
        manager.save()
        save_progress_figure(epoch + 1)
        print(f'--- epoch {epoch + 1} done, checkpoint saved ({(time.time() - session_start) / 60:.0f} min this session)')

TRAINING_COMPLETE = int(EPOCH.numpy()) >= EPOCHS
print('training complete' if TRAINING_COMPLETE else 'training NOT complete')

import pandas as pd

hist = pd.read_csv(LOG_PATH)
if len(hist):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.5))
    window = max(1, len(hist) // 50)
    x = hist['update']
    axes[0].plot(x, hist['loss'], alpha=0.3, color='C0')
    axes[0].plot(x, hist['loss'].rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean(), color='C0')
    axes[0].set(title='total loss (sum of 6 outputs)', xlabel='update', yscale='log')
    for k in ['dsn1', 'dsn2', 'dsn3', 'dsn4', 'dsn5', 'fuse']:
        axes[1].plot(x, (hist[k] / hist['chance']).rolling(window, min_periods=1).mean(), label=k)
    axes[1].axhline(1, color='gray', ls='--', lw=1)
    axes[1].set(title='loss per output / chance level (1 = guessing)', xlabel='update')
    axes[1].legend()
    axes[2].plot(x, hist['lr'])
    axes[2].set(title='learning rate', xlabel='update', yscale='log')
    for ax in axes:
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / 'training_curves.png', dpi=100)
    plt.show()

7. Export weights for hed-tensor¶

  • hed_bsds500.weights.h5: drop-in replacement for hed_tensor/weights/hed_bsds500.weights.h5.
  • hed_caffe_layout.npz: the same numbers under the original Caffe layer names (conv1_1/W, score-dsn1/b, new-score-weighting/W, ...). Kernels are Keras HWIO; for PyTorch use W.transpose(3, 2, 0, 1).
  • hed_config.json: preprocessing and training settings.
In [9]:
import json

WEIGHTS_FILE = EXPORT / 'hed_bsds500.weights.h5'
model.save_weights(WEIGHTS_FILE)

CAFFE_CONV_NAMES = ['conv1_1', 'conv1_2', 'conv2_1', 'conv2_2', 'conv3_1', 'conv3_2', 'conv3_3',
                    'conv4_1', 'conv4_2', 'conv4_3', 'conv5_1', 'conv5_2', 'conv5_3']
named = list(zip(CAFFE_CONV_NAMES, [l for blk in model.blocks() for l in blk.layers if isinstance(l, layers.Conv2D)]))
named += [(f'score-dsn{k}', dsn) for k, dsn in enumerate(model.dsns(), 1)] + [('new-score-weighting', model.fuse)]
np.savez(EXPORT / 'hed_caffe_layout.npz', **{f'{n}/{p}': getattr(l, a).numpy()
                                              for n, l in named for p, a in (('W', 'kernel'), ('b', 'bias'))})

hist = pd.read_csv(LOG_PATH)
CONFIG = {
    'model': 'HED (Xie & Tu, ICCV 2015), VGG16 backbone, TensorFlow/Keras',
    'weights_file': WEIGHTS_FILE.name,
    'compatible_with': 'hed-tensor (hed_tensor.HED: block1-5, dsn1-5, fuse)',
    'input': {'layout': 'NHWC', 'color_order': 'BGR', 'mean_bgr': MEAN_BGR.tolist(),
              'pixel_range': '0-255 minus mean, no scaling', 'size': 'any H x W'},
    'output': 'sigmoid(fuse), H x W x 1 in [0, 1]; call(training=True) gives the 6 logits',
    'npz_layout': 'Keras HWIO kernels; PyTorch Conv2d weight = W.transpose(3, 2, 0, 1)',
    'training': {
        'complete': TRAINING_COMPLETE, 'epochs_done': int(EPOCH.numpy()), 'updates_done': int(UPDATE.numpy()),
        'images_per_update': BATCH_SIZE, 'base_lr': BASE_LR, 'lr_step_updates': LR_STEP_UPDATES, 'lr_gamma': LR_GAMMA,
        'momentum': MOMENTUM, 'weight_decay': WEIGHT_DECAY, 'label_threshold': LABEL_THRESHOLD,
        'lr_mult': {'conv1-4': 1, 'conv5': 100, 'dsn': 0.01, 'fuse': 0.001, 'bias': '2x weight'},
        'dataset': f'HED-BSDS augmented train set, {len(pairs):,} pairs',
        'final_fuse_loss_vs_chance': round(float(hist['fuse'].iloc[-1] / hist['chance'].iloc[-1]), 4) if len(hist) else None,
        'smoke_test': SMOKE_TEST,
    },
    'environment': {'tensorflow': tf.__version__, 'keras': keras.__version__, 'gpus': GPU_NAMES,
                    'date': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')},
}
(EXPORT / 'hed_config.json').write_text(json.dumps(CONFIG, indent=2))

Check: the exported file loads in hed-tensor and gives the same output¶

The library prints a warning instead of failing when weights don't load, so this compares actual outputs.

In [10]:
lib_model = hed_tensor.HED(pretrained=False, weights=str(WEIGHTS_FILE))
_, x = load_test(TEST_PATHS[0])
diff = float(np.abs(lib_model(x, training=False).numpy() - model(x, training=False).numpy()).max())
print(f'max difference library vs notebook model: {diff:.2e}')
assert diff < 1e-5, 'exported weights did not load correctly into hed_tensor.HED'
del lib_model

8. Predict the 200 BSDS500 test images¶

Fused output and the 5 side outputs as PNGs (BSDS benchmark format), zipped in predictions/. Comparison with other models is done separately.

In [11]:
def save_map(prob, path):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Image.fromarray(np.round(np.clip(prob, 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(path)


t0 = time.time()
for path in TEST_PATHS:
    maps = [m.numpy()[0, ..., 0] for m in predict_all(load_test(path)[1])]
    save_map(maps[-1], PRED / 'fuse' / f'{path.stem}.png')
    for k, m in enumerate(maps[:5], 1):
        save_map(m, PRED / f'dsn{k}' / f'{path.stem}.png')
print(f'{len(TEST_PATHS)} test images in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s')

(WORK / 'predictions').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
shutil.make_archive(str(WORK / 'predictions' / 'ours_fuse'), 'zip', PRED / 'fuse')
shutil.make_archive(str(WORK / 'predictions' / 'ours_all_outputs'), 'zip', PRED)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 7, figsize=(21, 7.5))
for r, path in enumerate(TEST_PATHS[:3]):
    panels = [load_test(path)[0]] + [np.array(Image.open(PRED / n / f'{path.stem}.png'))
                                     for n in ['dsn1', 'dsn2', 'dsn3', 'dsn4', 'dsn5', 'fuse']]
    for c, (p, title) in enumerate(zip(panels, ['image', 'dsn1', 'dsn2', 'dsn3', 'dsn4', 'dsn5', 'fuse'])):
        axes[r, c].imshow(p if c == 0 else 255 - p, cmap=None if c == 0 else 'gray', vmin=0, vmax=255)
        axes[r, c].axis('off')
        if r == 0:
            axes[r, c].set_title(title)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG_DIR / 'side_outputs.png', dpi=90)
plt.show()
